# Results

*Generated by `scripts/build_results.py` from the JSON reports in `data/evaluation/`. Do not edit by hand.*

**Read this first.** Every figure below comes from synthetic tickets written by this project's own generator, and the knowledge articles and their relevance labels were written by the same author (an AI assistant) and have not been reviewed by a person. These results show that the pipelines work and how they compare with each other on this data. They do **not** establish accuracy, time savings or usefulness on real helpdesk tickets.

## 1. Ticket category classification

Dataset: 383 synthetic tickets (seed 42, sha256 `9c985c19b08d`). Primary split (new wording of known problems): train 191, validation 95, test 97. Model and settings were chosen on validation only; the test set was scored once.

| Model | Test accuracy | 95% interval | Macro-F1 | 95% interval | Accuracy on unseen problem types |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Majority class (floor) | 13.4% | 0.07 to 0.21 | 0.029 | 0.02 to 0.04 | 12.7% |
| TF-IDF + logistic regression (deployed) | 63.9% | 0.55 to 0.73 | 0.599 | 0.50 to 0.68 | 44.4% |
| TF-IDF + linear SVM | 69.1% | 0.60 to 0.78 | 0.683 | 0.58 to 0.77 | 46.0% |

Logistic regression minus SVM, paired difference in accuracy: -0.053 (95% interval -0.11 to 0.01). Interval includes 0 => no reliable difference at this sample size.

**Confidence threshold (0.5, chosen on validation).** On test, the deployed model auto-suggests for 36.1% of tickets, correct 97.1% of those times; 62 tickets are flagged for manual review, which catches 34 of its 35 errors. Calibration error (ECE) 0.147. Latency about 2.23 ms per ticket.

## 2. Retrieval: similar incidents and knowledge articles

Semantic scorer: **lsa** (a local latent-semantic stand-in; the pretrained sentence-embedding model could not be downloaded in the build environment and was never run).

**Similar incidents** (97 primary-split test tickets against 191 primary-split train tickets; a result is correct only if it is from the same scenario).

| Method | Precision@1 | Recall@3 | Recall@5 | MRR (95% interval) | nDCG@5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyword (TF-IDF) | 0.340 | 0.316 | 0.434 | 0.454 (0.37 to 0.54) | 0.414 |
| Semantic | 0.361 | 0.320 | 0.449 | 0.462 (0.38 to 0.55) | 0.429 |
| Hybrid | 0.351 | 0.323 | 0.444 | 0.458 (0.38 to 0.55) | 0.424 |

**Knowledge articles** (69 test tickets with a labelled article against 32 original sample articles; labels written by the project author).

| Method | Precision@1 | Recall@3 | Recall@5 | MRR (95% interval) | nDCG@5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Keyword (TF-IDF) | 0.971 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.986 (0.96 to 1.00) | 0.989 |
| Semantic | 0.971 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.986 (0.96 to 1.00) | 0.989 |
| Hybrid | 0.971 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.986 (0.96 to 1.00) | 0.989 |

Intervals overlap between methods, so no method is shown to be better than another. The article numbers are likely optimistic because the same author wrote articles and labels.

**Weak-match threshold for articles (hybrid, 0.5217).** Answers 84.1% of tickets that have a matching article (100.0% correct) but still suggests an article for 4 of 28 tickets that have none. No similarity threshold reached 80% precision for similar incidents.

## 3. Troubleshooting assistant

97 test tickets (69 with a matching article, 28 without). The assistant copies cited steps from approved articles and declines when the best article is below the validated threshold.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Right call (correct cited steps, or declined when no article exists) | 84.5% (95% interval 77.3% to 90.7%) |
| Offered steps when a matching article exists | 84.1% |
| Top article correct when it offered steps | 100.0% |
| Wrongly declined when an article exists | 11 |
| Declined when no article exists | 24 of 28 |
| Past resolution from the same scenario | 54.6% |

This measures choosing and citing the right article. It does not measure whether following the steps resolves a ticket.

## 4. Incident-burst detection

Rule: 5 or more tickets in one category within 3 hours (fixed in advance, not tuned). On the main dataset it found 2 of 2 generator-planted bursts with 0 false alarms (ticket recall 100.0%, precision 100.0%). Across 20 other generator seeds it found 40 of 40 bursts with 0 false alarms. The planted bursts are tight one-morning clusters, so this is an easy test.

## 5. Where AI helps, and where a person is still needed (measured)

| Task | What the AI does | What a person still does | Measured evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Category | Suggests a category with a confidence | Reviews and approves; all tickets below the threshold (62 of 97 on test) | Confident suggestions correct 97.1% on 36.1% of tickets; accuracy 63.9% overall, 44.4% on unseen problem types |
| Related articles | Ranks approved articles | Decides whether an article fits; writes and approves articles | Recall@5 1.00 (author-labelled, likely optimistic) |
| Troubleshooting | Shows cited steps, or says evidence is insufficient | Follows or ignores the steps; resolves the ticket | Right call 84.5%; effect on resolution not measured |
| Incident spotting | Flags bursts of tickets in one category | Confirms and declares an incident | 2 of 2 planted bursts found, 0 false alarms |

Live acceptance, correction and rating figures from technicians appear on the AI evaluation page and are not in this file, because they depend on the database in use.

## 6. What has not been measured

- Accuracy on real tickets (no real data is used).
- Time saved per ticket or change in resolution time.
- Whether technicians find the suggestions useful (needs a study with real users; ratings are collected for this).
- The pretrained sentence-embedding model and a sentence-embedding classifier (the model could not be downloaded in the build environment).
- Fairness, long-term drift, or behaviour under unusual ticket text.
- Any benefit claim such as cost savings: these are hypotheses until measured.

## 7. Reproducing these numbers

```bash
python scripts/train_classifier.py
python scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py
python scripts/evaluate_assistant.py
python scripts/evaluate_incidents.py
python scripts/build_results.py
```

Latency figures vary between runs and machines; all other figures are reproducible and checked by the test suite.
